title: Math functions compute in DOUBLE, also for FLOAT
verdict: fp32 inputs widen to DOUBLE and the result is DOUBLE; `round(FLOAT)` stays FLOAT
description: `sqrt`, `exp`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `atan2`, `power`, `ln`, `log`, `log10` and `log2` each have one signature, of DOUBLE to DOUBLE. A FLOAT argument is cast to DOUBLE, which is exact (`TryCastWithOverflowCheck(float, double)` is a plain conversion), and the result is a DOUBLE: one libm call on doubles, rounded once to binary64. DuckDB has no binary32 version of these functions, so a FLOAT input gets the fp64 answer.

The bodies are C++ `<cmath>` (`std::log`, `std::log10`, `std::log2`, `std::sqrt`, …) on doubles, so their rounding is the platform libm's, which is faithful but not always correctly rounded. `log(b, x)` is `log10(x) / log10(b)`, two roundings and a division.

Domain and log of zero for FLOAT inputs are those of DOUBLE (duckdb-R15-math-domain): with `ieee_floating_point_ops` on, NaN outside the domain and `-inf` for a logarithm of 0; with it off, `cannot take logarithm of zero`, `… of a negative number`, `ASIN is undefined outside [-1,1]`, and `sin`, `cos`, `tan` of `±inf` raise.

`round` has FLOAT overloads. `round(FLOAT)` rounds half away from zero, exact for a float; `round(FLOAT, d)` widens to double, computes `round(x · 10^d) / 10^d` there, and converts back to FLOAT, so it rounds twice (to binary64, then binary32). `inf` and NaN return the input.
reference: The elementary functions and logarithms of `fp32` would round to binary32 (`rounding: TIE_TO_EVEN`); `on_domain_error` and `on_log_zero` are `ERROR`. Lean refuses arithmetic on FLOAT values (duckdb-R12), so a plan casts them to DOUBLE first, which is what DuckDB does itself. For `fp64` the reference is Lean's native `Float`, also a libm call.

evidence.note: BindIEEEFloatingUnary/Binary: UnaryFunction<double, double, …>, BinaryFunction<double, double, double, …>
sqrt: DOUBLE only; raises on a negative input with ieee_floating_point_ops off
ln, log10, log(b, x), log2: DOUBLE only; std::log, std::log10, std::log2; zero and negative inputs raise with ieee_floating_point_ops off
sin, cos, tan (NoInfiniteDoubleWrapper), asin, atan, atan2, acos: DOUBLE only
RoundOperatorPrecision and RoundOperator: computed in double, LossyNumericCast to the result type
round: FLOAT overloads instantiate the operators at float
for FLOAT and DOUBLE with ieee_floating_point_ops = false: sqrt(-1), ln(-1), asin(2), acos(2), atanh(2), sin, cos, tan and cot of inf, cot(0), gamma(0) and lgamma(0) raise
with it on: sqrt, ln, log10 and log2 of -1 → nan; ln, log10 and log2 of 0 → -inf; asin(2), acos(2), atanh(2) → nan; sin, cos, tan, cot of inf → nan
CompareValues: numeric results are cast to the column type and compared with Value::ValuesAreEqual
ApproxEqual: NaN equals NaN, non-finite values compare exactly, finite ones within 1 %

provenance.notes: The arguments are FLOAT in the first iteration (`-1::FLOAT`, `'inf'::FLOAT`), so these settle `on_domain_error` of `fp.elem` and `fp.log` and `on_log_zero` at fp32. The runner compares FLOAT and DOUBLE results within 1 % and counts NaN equal to NaN of either sign and `-0.0` equal to `0.0` (`test/sqlite/result_helper.cpp`, `ApproxEqual` in `src/common/types.cpp`); infinities, integers, booleans and strings compare exactly. No test pins a last digit, so the `rounding` rows stay at the source reading.
